well: IODP Hole 343-C0019E - JAPAN TRENCH plate-boundary decollement, offshore Tohoku (37.938905 N, 143.913473 E; seafloor -6,887.5 m - the DEEPEST-WATER site in scientific ocean drilling and the deepest-water entry in this catalogue by a factor of 2.5); JFAST (Japan Trench Fast Drilling Project), Expedition 343, May 2012, thirteen months after the 2011 Mw 9.0 Tohoku-oki earthquake whose shallow fault slip (~50 m reaching the trench) this hole was drilled to sample; 21 cores, 137 m cored, 43% recovered, 844.5 m penetrated
operator_on_log: Ikari, Ito, Ujiie & Kopf (MARUM/Tohoku Univ./Univ. Tsukuba) laboratory shearing experiments on core 17R-1 from the plate-boundary fault zone, driven at PLATE-TECTONIC RATES (~cm/yr class); drilling by D/V CHIKYU - the catalogue's second Chikyu entry and second Ikari-lab entry (companion discipline to the Nankai megasplay shear-strength table)
source_database: PANGAEA, dataset doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.858800 ('Slow slip event measurements of IODP Hole 343-C0019'); supplement to Ikari et al. 2015, Nature Geoscience 8(11), 870-874 (doi:10.1038/ngeo2547)
license: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported (CC-BY-3.0), declared IN the file's own header. Attribution: Ikari/Ito/Ujiie/Kopf / PANGAEA / IODP
fetch_method: read-only HTTPS fetch of the PANGAEA textfile export - COMPLETE dataset (83 data points per the header's own Size declaration = 23 label cells + 60 numeric cells across 7 experiment rows x 16 columns) in one fetch
coverage: COMPLETE DATASET: 7 laboratory experiments on Tohoku plate-boundary fault-zone material (sample 343-C0019E-17R-1, intact and powdered), of which FIVE produced spontaneous laboratory SLOW SLIP EVENTS (loadup 19,556-74,138 s; shear-stress drops 51.1-121.9 kPa = 2.95-6.54% of the 1,703.2-1,865.8 kPa peak strengths; friction-coefficient drops 0.007-0.017; slip distances 25.3-61.9 um over durations 7,310-14,580 s; sliding velocities 0.0005-0.0079 um/s) and TWO refused ('*no SSE', carried verbatim with all twelve numeric fields empty) - a negative result preserved as data
curves: ordinal experiment index (no depth geocode - the catalogue's label-indexed PANGAEA route)
V [µm/s] (mininum velocity) + V [µm/s] (maximum velocity) (source spelling 'mininum' preserved verbatim)
Exp rides as per-sample quality; Sample label/comment + '*no SSE' Comment verbatim in file
source_anomaly_disclosure: TWO source quirks preserved verbatim: (1) the header parameter comment spells 'mininum velocity' (source typo, untouched); (2) experiment B379 run 1's mean slip velocity, Distance/Duration = 46.7/11510.0 = 0.00406 um/s, EXCEEDS its own reported maximum sliding velocity 0.0032 um/s - the other four SSE rows all keep Distance/Duration inside their reported [V_min, V_max] band; the inconsistency is the archive's, detected by re-deriving the band check, and carried unchanged with this disclosure
purpose: thirty-first catalogue entry - a TRIPLE FIRST: the JAPAN TRENCH joins as region NINETEEN, laboratory SLOW-SLIP-EVENT friction measurements are kind TWENTY (the time-dependent counterpart to the Nankai monotonic shear-strength table: not how strong the fault is, but HOW it fails), and at -6,887.5 m seafloor it sets the catalogue's water-depth record; the material is the actual plate-boundary gouge that hosted the 2011 Tohoku Mw 9.0 - the paper's headline physics (slow slip events nucleate spontaneously in this material at plate-tectonic loading rates, with tiny stress drops on a weak fault) is re-derived from the table by the gate on every run
verified: 83 non-empty body cells against the header's own Size declaration (23 label + 60 numeric, EXACT); stress-drop identity Perc = Tau_drop/Shear_str_max x 100 re-derived on all 5 SSE rows within input-rounding (<=0.02 pct); slow-slip character pinned (all V_max <= 0.0079 um/s - five orders below seismic slip rates - with durations 2-4 h); 4-of-5 mean-velocity band check + the B379-run-1 exceedance pinned as disclosed; the two '*no SSE' rows load as all-NaN numerics with Comment verbatim; gate-pinned; source URL serves the identical dataset
